prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: B036 remains the strongest case on the shortlist, and the round-1 exchange has strengthened it because no member questioned its maturity or its content. The discovery is specific and its effect on medicine is discernible: proglucagon processing, the biologically active truncated GLP-1 peptides, human incretin physiology with glucose-dependent insulin secretion, and central effects on appetite, followed by therapies whose benefit has been confirmed in large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. I keep a single-part prize on Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The chair asks whether the citation rewards the physiology or the creation of long-acting drugs. I hold that it should reward the discovery of what the hormone is, which form is active and what it does, with the therapeutic consequence named in the citation as the outcome and not as the credited achievement. A second part is not needed: no other shortlisted candidate combines stable interpretation, clean attribution and clear impact well enough to stand beside it, and the three-person limit is already fully used.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution and I do not want to hide it. Habener is outside the credited names yet has a real claim to the early proglucagon and peptide work, and every member says so. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide is contested and none of us has verified it against the supplied evidence, so my choice of her over Knudsen is a judgement about prize scope, not a settled finding of fact. Knudsen's analogue engineering is what put these drugs in patients, and a committee that weights transformation of care equally with discovery could reasonably prefer her in the third place. If the Habener omission is accepted, it should be recorded in the deliberation and the citation worded around the physiology and the active peptides, not around priority for one finding.

responses.point: Sandberg says the missing Habener credit is a real weakness and, if peptide-identification credit cannot be assigned fairly from the names supplied, the Mojsov slot weakens and Knudsen should be revisited.
responses.response: I accept the logic and have tested it. Without Habener the physiology side has two firm anchors, Holst for human incretin physiology and Drucker for mechanisms and tissue action, and the supplied material places Mojsov's contribution on the identity of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, which is the step that links the early peptide work to a usable hormone. Even if her priority is contested, dropping her would leave the active-peptide discovery unrepresented, whereas dropping Knudsen leaves a development achievement outside the citation but acknowledged by its wording. So I do not move to Knudsen. My condition is that if members show from the evidence that the active-peptide credit belongs elsewhere, Knudsen becomes the better third name than leaving the slot to a weakly supported one. On the evidence I have, I keep Mojsov.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Knudsen to Mojsov but says that if the Committee values transformation of care as much as discovery, his opening configuration would be better, and he suggests the unfolded protein response as a cleaner alternative if GLP-1 allocation stalls.
responses.response: I agree that this is the one real fork. The Nobel criterion as I read it is a discovery that changes a field, and for B036 the change in the field began with the physiology; the engineering of long-acting analogues followed from it. I do not think the allocation has stalled, because the objection to Mojsov is about the strength of a priority claim and not about whether the achievement is the right one. On B006 I would use it as the alternative if the GLP-1 trio cannot be defended, since Mori and Walter are a clean pair with a clear mechanism. I would not use it as a second part, because the three-person limit already holds Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and adding two names breaks the cap.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, asks whether foundational work outside the credited names weakens B026, B031 and B047, and whether the same principle should be applied consistently to B036.
responses.response: The principle should be applied consistently, and that is why I treat B036 differently. In B026 and B031 the missing work is the foundational causal discovery, the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion, or TNF cloning and antibody engineering, and the credited names would be read as rewarding the clinical step. In B036 the credited trio contains the discovery side: Holst, Drucker and Mojsov cover human incretin physiology, mechanism and the active peptide. What is missing is Habener, one contributor to early peptide work, and this is a smaller gap than a missing foundation. I therefore do not think the consistency test removes B036, but I support recording Habener's position openly, and I think the same test is why I keep B026 below B006.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would pair B036 with B031 or B047 as a possible second part and treats anti-TNF as mature and unusually well attributed.
responses.response: I have reconsidered B031 as a second part. It is mature and the Feldmann-Maini attribution is clean, but with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov already named, a second part would add two more people and exceed the three-person limit; a pair of laureates in one part and three in another cannot be combined here. If the Committee dropped Mojsov to leave room, I would be removing the discoverer side of B036 to make way for a candidate whose conceptual claim, in my view, still rests on TNF biology and antibody engineering outside the pair. I remain unpersuaded that this is better than a single strong part, and I do not change my position, but I take seriously that anti-TNF is a future option.

responses.point: El-Manira names optogenetics (B042) as a leading alternative and treats B036's physiology-centred trio as better than a company-development framing.
responses.response: We agree on the B036 framing. On B042 I share your reservations that it is a method and that six names must be cut to three, and Linnarsson's point that a channelrhodopsin part would need Nagel and Hegemann plus a neuronal-application name makes it harder. Impact on circuit neuroscience is not in doubt, and I keep B042 as an alternative because the field change is specific and visible. But I could not support it as a second part while the cap leaves no room, and as a replacement for B036 it would need a defensible three-name reduction that I have not seen in the file.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is correctly weighed against Habener, who is not credited, and against Knudsen.
Whether the Committee wants a citation anchored in physiology or one that includes the creation of long-acting drugs, which determines the third name.
Whether the three-person limit makes any second part impossible in practice, since B006 and B031 add two names each and B042 or B047 add at least three.
My recollection of exact priority and chronology for the GLP-1 peptide work is from memory and not verified against the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No specific conflict with any credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my profile. My nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans and my collaborations with Johan Ericson, Per Svenningsson and Abdel El Manira involve no credited name, and shared institution or topic is not treated as a personal tie. No round-1 statement raised a tie involving me and a credited name.
